name: 13 Kensington Palace Gardens
scope: Model the named Gothic residence with its entrance tower, brick/stone facade and conservatory. It is a separate building from Kensington Palace.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

review.method: Original public-domain architect illustrations plus primary Survey of London alteration history and statutory heritage description; native map and independent ground retained.
review.notes: Full surviving residence and south conservatory accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi scope. Cleared Qualla media checked first; only the modern attribution-only facade and unrelated Kensington Palace map were published, so neither is active imagery. Two exact public-domain original illustrations from architect C.J.Richardson’s The Englishman’s House were individually inspected: complete exterior perspective p476 and ground plan p479. The primary Gutenberg catalog explicitly marks the book public domain in the USA and identifies Richardson1806–1871; the selected image links, catalog/book snapshots and exact bytes are bound. The drawings establish the sash-window wings, projecting central oriel/entry, open parapets, chimney rhythm and side conservatory. Primary Survey of London1973text independently describes the surviving buff-brick/Bath-stone body and1924alterations: bell turret removed, steps/wooden porch changed, conservatory windows changed and its sloping roof replaced by flat roof. That flat-roof statement applies to the conservatory, not a surveyed description of the entire main roof. Historic England1266971 independently identifies the symmetrical Gothic facade, diagonal buttresses, sash openings, central oriel and entrance canopy. Existing geometry agrees at medium-fi scope; historical turret is correctly omitted. No original scope removed or geometry rebuilt. Precise tracery, doorway/porch profiles, secondary openings, main-roof slopes/drainage, conservatory glazing subdivisions and current fixtures remain estimates. Original native footprint, heading, independent ground and source/runtime/four LOD bytes retained. Fourteen current portable/shared views inspected and retained; fresh current-identity detail/LOD frames required before completion. No reference pixels embedded.

originalReview.notes: Complete original exterior perspective individually inspected: two-storey sash-window wings, projecting central entrance/oriel tower, open patterned parapets, corner piers and chimney stacks. Historical bell turret and upper cap differ from the surviving state and are not restored.

Complete original ground plan individually inspected. Confirms central hall/saloon and rear gallery, flanking wings, projecting entry and south-side conservatory. Old internal partitions/stable yard are outside the exterior model; the historical plan is not treated as a current measured survey.
